speaker: Doctor
text:
Have you noticed any specific triggers for these episodes, such as flashing lights, sudden noises, or strong emotions?

REQUEST TEST: EEG (Electroencephalogram) to evaluate for abnormal brain activity.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Patient
text: c and confused afterwards. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the clarification; confusion afterwards is indeed common after a seizure. However, since your previous doctor suspected Multiple Sclerosis, have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your limbs, or any issues with your vision?

REQUEST TEST: MRI of the brain and spinal cord to rule out demyelinating lesions characteristic of Multiple Sclerosis.
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain_and_Spine

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Brain: No evidence of mass lesions, infarctions, or structural abnormalities. MRI_Spine: No evidence of demyelinating lesions characteristic of Multiple Sclerosis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
With the MRI ruling out Multiple Sclerosis and no structural abnormalities found, have you or anyone else witnessed what your eyes or body were doing specifically during those unresponsive spells?

REQUEST TEST: Video_EEG_monitoring to capture an episode and correlate clinical signs with electrical brain activity.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Video_EEG monitoring captured a 2.5-minute episode of staring, automatisms (hand rubbing), and unresponsiveness. Concurrent electroencephalogram showed a rhythmic 3-Hz spike-and-wave pattern generalizing from the right temporal region to both hemispheres, consistent with generalized tonic-clonic seizure activity originating in the right temporal lobe.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Temporal Lobe Epilepsy. The presence of a 3-Hz spike-and-wave pattern generalizing from the right temporal lobe, coupled with automatisms (hand rubbing) and post-ictal confusion, is pathognomonic for this condition, effectively ruling out Multiple Sclerosis.
